_about: Machine-readable encoding of every 'no X' rule from the Olive & Vine design system. A future lint hook (CI step, pre-commit, or audit script) can consume this file: walk each rule's `patterns` against the matching `targets` glob, ignore anything in `exceptions`, and report by `severity`. Keep the rationale on every rule — drift starts when 'why' gets lost.

rules.name: No box-shadow or text-shadow anywhere
rules.rationale: Hover state and depth are communicated through color swap and the NE corner gesture, never through shadow. README §3: 'unusually disciplined for a contemporary site — there are no box-shadows on cards.' Adding a shadow is the most common drift path back into generic SaaS visual language.

rules.name: No backdrop-filter / blur
rules.rationale: No frosted-glass surfaces. The brand uses opacity layering at documented tiers (30/50/70/80), never a blur filter on a backdrop.

rules.name: No mix-blend-mode (scrim faking)
rules.rationale: Hover state is color-swap, not blend-mode darkening. The site.html legacy used mix-blend-mode: multiply as a scrim on a video hero — exactly the failure mode Direction B prohibits.

rules.name: No multi-hue gradient as a brand surface
rules.rationale: The only permitted gradient is the single-hue radial vignette documented in Decision C (deep-olive base + leaf-pale wash at low opacity). Any other gradient — multi-hue, scrim-darkening, or texture — falls back to the F08 abstract-gradient hero mistake the rebuild was meant to fix.

exceptions._note: radial-gradient is allowed when it uses ONLY the single-hue stops from useHeroLight or playbook-documented vignettes. A second-stage lint should validate the stops; this rule only forbids linear/conic.

rules.name: No hex color outside the documented olive + ink + cream token set
rules.rationale: The brand is a single olive hue plus ink/cream/charcoal/paper. The historical purple (#B08FCA) and yellow (#B5A332) in the tax timeline categories was the F04 violation Decision B cleaned up; this rule prevents reintroduction.

values_allowlist._note: Top row = Direction-B brand olives. Second row = Decision-G per-service hero-base tints (--ov-olive-rooted/-hearth/-steady). Anything outside this list in app/ source is a finding.

rules.name: No unicode glyph as an icon (arrows, bullets, checks, stars)
rules.rationale: The icon vocabulary is react-icons SVG components only. Substituting → / ✓ / • / ★ as text characters reverts to generic typography and breaks the stroke-weight discipline.

exceptions._note: Source-code comments are excluded — only flag occurrences inside JSX text or string literals destined for rendering. A path-aware lint should walk the AST and skip Comment nodes.

rules.name: No emoji anywhere in user-facing copy
rules.rationale: The site uses zero emoji in product copy or UI. This is part of the partnership voice — emoji read as casual / consumer, not as a professional advisory firm.

rules.name: No lorem ipsum / TODO / placeholder strings shipped
rules.rationale: F01 was lorem ipsum Korean under the Tax timeline. Shipping placeholder text again is the one unacceptable outcome the brief calls out by name.

exceptions._note: TODO/FIXME inside source comments is fine; lint should walk AST and skip Comment nodes when checking these two.

rules.name: No italic used as a recurring brand emphasis pattern
rules.rationale: Italic is allowed only where Roboto's italic naturally appears in editorial body copy (e.g. a book title). It is not a recurring headline device.
rules._severity_note: This rule produces many false positives (the word 'italic' in comments, prop names, etc). Treat hits as candidates for human review, not auto-fail.

rules.name: No corner radii outside the documented vocabulary
rules.system_ref: README.md#3-visual-foundations -> Corner radii — the signature gesture
rules.rationale: Radii are: 0 (default), 30px (card NE-on-hover), 300px (insight card NE-on-hover), pill (9999px buttons/dots only). Random arbitrary radii (e.g. rounded-lg, rounded-xl) dilute the signature gesture.

rules.name: Hero cursor-follow light must use the shared useHeroLight hook
rules.rationale: Forking the easing loop per page guarantees drift across the six service heroes. The hook owns the gradient string, the lerp factor, and the accessibility fallbacks — page code should only pass its resting `defaultX/Y`.

exceptions._note: The SSR initial-state inline style is permitted (it mirrors what useHeroLight will paint once mounted). A second-stage lint should validate the inline matches the hook's canonical string.

rules.name: Service motion icons must use the ServiceIconMotion component
rules.rationale: Inline-authoring the SVG markup per page guarantees the six icons drift apart on stroke widths, durations, and color treatments. The single component owns all six.

rules.name: No mp4 video or PNG-sequence sprite for the hero motion
rules.rationale: The mp4 + PNG-sequence exports in audits/assets/ov-service-icons/ are RGB without alpha — they would show a visible white box on the dark hero. Using mix-blend-mode to fake transparency violates Decision B. Only the inline SVG path is approved.

rules.name: No invented client names, ticker copy, or [00] mono labels as a pattern
rules.rationale: The site.html legacy invented client names ('Cathay Provisions Group', 'Hansol Capital Partners') and used `[ 00 ]` mono-font section numbers as an editorial-agency device. Both are voice violations.

rules.name: The Pattern-05 4×3 month grid must be hidden below md
rules.rationale: A 12-cell grid below 768px collapses into either a 1×12 column (worse than the cards) or a 2×6 grid (loses the calendar metaphor). The cards already carry the same data better on phone.
rules._severity_note: Implementation-defined check; requires AST awareness, not regex.

rules.name: Calendar category colors must all be within the olive token family
rules.rationale: The historical purple (#B08FCA) and yellow (#B5A332) category colors were the F04 violation. Categories must use olive tints only — the no-non-token-hex rule covers this, but it's worth a dedicated rule because category-color is a deliberate decision point.

rules.name: Every user-facing string must have both `en` and `ko` halves
rules.rationale: The site is bilingual; the codebase uses `{ en, ko }` objects for every rendered string. Drift starts when someone ships an English-only string.
rules._severity_note: AST check; not regex-implementable. Listed for completeness.
